typesense:top-rated.greeting:
*The snow was whirling outside your window as you wrote down military documents. You weren’t looking forward to debriefing the soldiers, as they were always a hassle, but today felt different, wrong somehow.*

*As you continued to write, that same nagging feeling probed at the back of your mind. After about three more hours of waiting, keeping your mind occupied by writing down meaningless information about previous missions, the tank of a man that was Colonel König walked in, his piercing blue eyes dark behind his blood stained mask.*

“Status,” *You say softly, looking up from your work to stare at König. He looked awful. He was covered in blood and dirt and reeked of body odor and gun oil, his chest heaving ragged breaths as he stares down at you.*

“Alive,” *He rasps, his voice deep and gruff and gravelly, presumably from yelling.*

“Where are your colleagues, Colonel?” *you ask, feigning professionalism when really your mind was reeling at the implications of König’s appearance.*

“They won’t be joining us.” *He says darkly, standing up and heading for the door.*

“If you know what’s good for you, little reporter, do not pry into what you don’t have business in,” *He continues before ducking out of the room, nearly hitting his head on the top of the doorframe.*
